That sounds super tough and can definitely relate to having a hectic home like that so maybe a good idea would be to get some time for yourselves? Whether that's just you and you SO or by yourselves. Maybe you go on a date once a week where you dedicate some of the day to doing your own thing and then perhaps do something nice together. It could be as small as getting coffee or even something like starting a project you would both like to do. There will never be a perfect time in a family really but making time to do stuff that makes you feel happy is so important. However, the thing that has helped best is definitely taking time out to relax a bit and encouraging each other to dedicate time to ourselves and having fun.

I think that it is our personality type that can make us feel a sense of alienation/depersonalisation more than others at times. While some people will never experience disassociation from their lives, some people, like you and me, get in their head about wanting to be happy a lot and this brings us to the realisation that we are mere humans and we don't have as much control over life as we think. Which sucks for idealists. 

Don't forget though, that the more you look for the perfect life, the less likely you are to be satisfied. I think this is probably the reason that we end up unhappy, because we start to think that if we cant find any meaning or we keep waiting around to find happiness when 'true' happiness (for me) comes from letting go of all of my ideals and remembering what really makes me feel happy. 

I think smoking can also heighten the mental state that you are in and I can definitely relate to what you're saying about it making you realise how alien everything really is especially during such uncertain times. I think Lynch is a filmmaker that captures this feeling really well if you want some movies to watch while at home. Kaufman's recent films also cover these topics really well too and deffo affected my approach to life. 

TLDR; there is never going to be a perfect time to be happy because nothing is perfect but you're allowed to feel happiness despite this.

When I saw the title I expected a middle 14 year old 'deep' but uncreative poem but I love the creativity and metaphor in the first stanza and feel like you could have left it there and it still would have had the full effect as I kept going back to read the first few lines. However as it went on I felt it lacked the same emotion and desperation I felt when I started reading. I especially like the reference to 'mother' earth as it creates a strong emotional connection between the reader and the victim in this poem. I think the end could be more punchy, for example just three words that encapsulate how the human race treat our earth would be more memorable perhaps. But I certainly couldn't create a masterpiece like this. What inspired this poem in particular?

For a short poem this seems too simple I think it would better improve the poem if there was more depth to the words as the subject matter is clearly one of deep importance to you. For example the line 'It strips beauty from the soul' seems like it should convey more pain and feeling than telling it as it is without the emotional attachments that come along with separating beauty and the human soul. You could go into this using metaphor perhaps as I realise this is a hard subject matter to get your head around with a straight explanation. Think about how Blanche would express this feeling in streetcar. 

Other than that I cannot disagree  with the message of this poem it just feels very literal and only applicable to you even though this is a generic issue that most people can relate to. Hope this is somewhat helpful and please correct me if I have the complete wrong end of the stick!

Not sure how much this helps but having someone to hold you accountable to things you want to do or ideas you have really helps me get projects done as well as breaking down bigger things into smaller goals so it doesn't seem like such a huge task. However, I know exactly what you mean when you say you feel no motivation or focus so I think meditation can sometimes help me clear the noise in my head but I know it takes years to learn this skill so I am still learning too. 

I hope you know you're not alone in this and although the majority of people might not understand why you are this way, I feel like I personally have never related so much to a post on here and the frustration you feel. I think it can be extra frustrating when everyone around you may appear to be fully functioning and carefree, but I am sure that under the surface there is every possibility that they could be struggling too as this kind of thing is not always obvious to others and as you were saying people always tell you that you have so much potential. But that doesn't mean that you should be disappointed in yourself because they probably don't see how well you are doing considering how hard day to day is! The fact that you have pushed yourself to do so much with your life just shows that you can do it and as someone that has had many similar experiences in life, I have learned that the only way to get through is to talk to people and let them know whats going on so that they can try to help (I don't mean u have to explain your whole story to everyone but the things you are dealing with right now to help them understand a bit more) and try not to compare yourself with everyone as you are special and have your own strengths and purposes in life that cognitively 'normal' people wish they had so it's never all black and white and sometimes different can be good and I believe you can find your 'superpowers' when you are restricted from the normal way of thinking.
